title: Indian heritage among musicians; Mildred's mother and stepmother
summary: Dance notes musicians with Native American ancestry; Norvo adds Lee Wiley and Joe Mondragon and recalls Mildred's mother dying young and her demonstrating songs in a music store.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Listen, on that score, don't mean to sidetrack you, but isn't it surprising the number of talented musicians that have got some Indian blood somewhere. I mean like Jack Teagarden comes to mind. Johnny Hodges had.
Who?

Johnny Hodges -- Johnny Hodges' grandmother was Indian. And Johnny, if you look at his face you could tell, you know, he had that heritage. And, there's an awful lot of musicians that have got that heritage and it's -- to me it's really surprising.
Well Lee Wiley had a little.
Did she?

Had a little Indian blood. I don't know how much, I think it was a sixteenth or something. And on the coast, one of the real good bass players was with Woody Herman that worked the studios for years, was Joe Mondragon.
OH.
He was Indian, from Colorado. There was a couple of wonderful musicians, good friend of Jimmy Rowles Rose up in Spokane, that were great musicians. John Benson (?)?
Yeah, well you know --
I don't think that-- I think that --
I mean, there's evidently a very fine musical heritage there.
Oh, I think so. I think -- yes, I don't know how to put my hand on it or --

No. Well neither do I -- I mean you can't -- if you look -- I mean as far as the music that you -- the little music that of Indian music that I've heard, well I would never have supposed there was this, but there evidently is, because you can spot it in musicians all over the place.
Yeah.
You know, and it's clearly there in Jack -- Teagarden.
Sure.

YOU know? Yeah, it's a -- well Mildred told me herself that -- that when she was real young and she was studying singing, or working, and that -- that her mother took her to meetings, song meetings and things.
Yeah.
She said she got very good training.
Oh, yeah. Yeah.
I suppose those intervals are different too.

Well her mother was quite well educated the way I understand it -- from the boys, too. You know they weren't as close to Mildred, I think that was a big shock in Mildred's life when her mother died so young.
Was it?
Yeah. Mildred was quite young. I don't know if Mildred was the oldest or not. I think Al was a little younger than Mildred. I'm not sure --
Oh, yeah.
But I know -- she used to tell me that she'd -- reason she left home, was she didn't get along with her stepmother.
Yeah. With her stepmother, yeah.
But then I know before she ever sang she was demonstrating songs in a music store.
Yeah. That's right --
Did she ever tell you about it?
Yes, I do remember, yes I do.
Uh-huh, had a piano -- she'd stand up and sing the songs, they handed her the songs --
Devils --
Yeah.
